subject: EU-only processing — operational proofs, support access, and deletion timeline
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Eva Müller <eva.mueller@meditech.de>, Meditech Legal <legal@meditech.de>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: EU-only processing — initial checklist and a few clarifying questions

Hi Eva / Meditech legal team,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I'm attaching a short checklist that maps the typical contractual and operational asks we see for EU-only processing requests. To make sure we scope precisely for Meditech, two clarifying questions up front: 

1) For your definition of “EU-only processing” — do you require the control plane to also reside in the EU, or is it sufficient that the data plane (model hosting, logs, backups) remains within EU regions while the control plane is hosted in our global control plane?

2) Can you confirm whether Meditech will accept Redwood-managed KMS keys with customer key rotation, or does the legal team require customer-held keys (BYOK) in your Azure/AWS account?

Operationally, the checklist highlights: in-region hosting, backup lifecycle (retention & deletion windows), privileged support access controls (just-in-time, session recording), and SCCs/Annexes to the DPA.

Attached: initial-sccs-checklist.xlsx — short mapping of asks to technical controls.

Next steps: if you can reply with answers to the two bullets above and any additional non-negotiable clauses, we’ll prepare a targeted Annex + proposed pilot (30-day retention window, deletion attestations).

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Director, Enterprise Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0133
From: Dr. Eva Müller <eva.mueller@meditech.de>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Meditech Legal <legal@meditech.de>
Date: 2028-08-14T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: EU-only processing — initial checklist and a few clarifying questions

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the checklist — that format is helpful. A few quick answers and follow-ups: 

- Control plane: Meditech’s minimum requirement is that customer data (including logs, backups, and any cached inference artifacts) are processed and stored only in EU jurisdictions. We prefer the control plane also be in-region, but will accept a global control plane provided contractual guarantees prevent cross-border configuration/exports and you can prove effective separation.

- KMS: Preference is for customer-held keys. If Redwood can demonstrate an audited BYOK flow where the keys never leave Meditech's KMS and Redwood cannot decrypt without Meditech's explicit operation, that will suffice.

- Support access: any remote support that could expose customer data must be strictly gated: JIT access, MFA, recorded session, and prior customer consent for each session. We need a support-access matrix showing which Redwood roles can request access and under what legal basis.

- Evidence: we will ask for deletion attestations, backup lifecycle logs, and a one-time proof-of-deletion test for a scoped dataset. Also we will need the SCCs with an Annex describing the technical controls and subprocessor list.

Can you provide a timeline for a redline of the DPA + a proposed pilot (pilot scope + attestation cadence)?

Regards,
Dr. Eva Müller
Head of Data Governance
Meditech GmbH
+49 30 1234 5678
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Eva Müller <eva.mueller@meditech.de>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-15T08:45:00Z
Subject: Re: EU-only processing — initial checklist and a few clarifying questions

Eva — thanks for the clear list. A technical sketch to map to the asks above: 

- Data plane: we can pin model serving, KV caches, logs, and backups to EU regions only (we run dedicated customer pools for this). Snapshots and object storage are restricted via region ACLs.

- Control plane: today our control plane is globally distributed for management/rollout reasons. We can offer a private control plane option (Private deployment) where the control plane is hosted in your VPC/region for an enterprise contract. Alternatively, we can keep the control plane global but implement strict role-based restrictions and contractual prohibition of config export; we’ll also provide a signed attestation and audit logs showing no export actions.

- KMS: we support BYOK via an HSM/KMS integration. With BYOK, Redwood never has the plaintext keys; we can support customer-run keys in AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault and require customer-driven rekey ops.

- Support access: we have a support-access matrix (attached as support-access-matrix.csv) that lists role-level privileges, required approvals, and session recording. For EU-only pilots we will add an extra approval gate with Meditech-designated approvers.

- Proof-of-deletion: we can run a scoped deletion test on a designated sandbox dataset and produce object-store deletion logs + snapshot hashes. For backups we can provide backup retention records and an incremental deletion trace.

I'll link our EU playbook with implementation patterns for the Private control plane and the BYOK flow here: https://redwood.example.com/security/eu-inregion-playbook

If that all looks acceptable, Naomi and I will draft the SCC Annex and a short technical Annex describing the pilot scope and attestation cadence. Proposed pilot: 30-day retention, one-time deletion proof at pilot end, and monthly deletion attestations during pilot.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Eva Müller <eva.mueller@meditech.de>, Meditech Legal <legal@meditech.de>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-16T10:20:00Z
Subject: Re: EU-only processing — initial checklist and a few clarifying questions

Eva — thanks. Marcus’s summary is accurate and actionable. Proposed next steps from Redwood: 

1) We will produce two artifacts by EOD 2028-08-18: (a) a draft SCC Annex + DPA redline that captures the control-plane options and BYOK language; (b) a proposed pilot runbook (30-day retention, scoped dataset, deletion proof steps and evidence types).

2) Technical deliverables: we will attach the in-region deletion procedure (inregion-deletion-procedure-v1.docx) and the support-access matrix CSV for your review.

3) Pilot gating: we request confirmation of the pilot dataset and two Meditech approvers for support JIT approvals. Can you confirm approver names and whether Meditech legal needs additional contractual language around audit-friendliness (e.g., ability to request artifact exports for 3rd-party auditors)?

Attached: inregion-deletion-procedure-v1.docx (procedure + logs/artefact types).

Naomi
Director, Enterprise Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Dr. Eva Müller <eva.mueller@meditech.de>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Meditech Legal <legal@meditech.de>
Date: 2028-08-18T15:36:00Z
Subject: Re: EU-only processing — initial checklist and a few clarifying questions

Naomi / Marcus — that timeline works for us. A few confirmations before you produce redlines: 

- Pilot dataset: Meditech will supply a scoped synthetic dataset (PHI-shaped) and designate two approvers: 
  - Eva Müller (Head of Data Governance)
  - Lukas Schmidt (Head of IT Security)

- Audit exports: Meditech will require the ability to request export artifacts for an agreed third-party auditor; please include that as an option in the Annex (scope + cadence restrictions).

- Deletion attestation cadence: for the pilot we want a one-time proof at pilot end + a monthly summary for the following two months. If pilot passes, cadence will move to quarterly.

Please proceed and send the draft DPA redline + Annex and pilot runbook. Once we have those we’ll confirm legal redlines and the timeline for a 4-week pilot start window.

Regards,
Dr. Eva Müller
Head of Data Governance
Meditech GmbH
